summary: Part 3 of the Planet Labs deep dive (published 2026-09-21) examines the sources of surging demand for Planet's satellite imagery. Governments urgently need sovereign space access, regional threat awareness, and defense modernization — especially as US allies feel they can no longer depend on the current US administration amid trade barriers and stepped-back alliances — driving triple-digit year-over-year revenue growth in Planet's Europe/Middle East/Africa segment. New contracts include a Rwanda Space Agency deal for high-resolution national data and analytics across agriculture, urban management, and disaster response. The creator's central question is whether demand extends beyond defense: drawing a parallel with Palantir, he wants evidence of enterprise adoption, since enterprise budgets could dwarf government spending and justify big upside. The commercial segment grew only 15% YoY (slowest of all categories), though a six-figure expanded renewal with a hyperscaler AI developer for monitoring data-center and semiconductor-fab construction hints at a template for enterprise use. He concludes enterprise adoption is still a few years away and the stock only makes sense if that upside materializes. Call: PL UNCERTAIN.
